decision: PROMISING narrowly for Givens-aligned logical experts; independent experts require free Tucker coefficients
facts: Aligned 128-expert bank: Mirror 4,555 B / routed NRMSE 4.95e-4; free Tucker 6,313 B / 2.97e-4 (~28% bytes saved); generic PCA 4,867 B / 3.52e-4.
All methods pay shared matrix bank and fixed dispatch metadata. Mirror is ~6.4% smaller than generic PCA but has slightly higher error; fit wall time ~4.0 ms vs PCA ~0.32 ms.
Expert forward is 256 MAC/token after materialization; Tucker/Mirror/PCA each use 262,144 one-time materialization MACs for all experts.
Independent coefficients: free Tucker NRMSE 2.93e-4; Mirror 1.037 and PCA 0.810.
interpretation: A Givens code can increase logical expert multiplicity over a shared Tucker bank and improve the storage-quality frontier against free Tucker coefficients in this aligned toy. Generic PCA occupies a nearby Pareto point; the result is not general MoE evidence. Independent expert functions need private coefficients.
hypothesis: Supported narrowly as aligned representation feasibility with a distinct storage-quality Pareto point; broad or natural MoE capacity is not established.
counter_hypothesis: Teacher coefficients are directly generated from the same Givens orbit, and generic PCA is nearly as compact/more accurate. A stronger nonlinear coefficient control could close the gap.
limitations: Fixed router is a deterministic balanced hash, not learned
Aligned coefficients generated from Mirror orbit
No LM/MoE training or route/task accuracy
One-time materialization cost counted analytically; no inference-latency benchmark
